climatic_reasoning: Relies on high diurnal thermal mass to smooth extreme day/night winter temperature swings in sub-zero Leh weather (-15?C night).
insulation_strategy: Heavy earthen mass provides moderate resistance (R_mat = 0.458 m?K/W for 465mm stone/adobe/plaster) supplemented by boundary air films (Rsi+Rse = 0.17 m?K/W).
thermal_mass_strategy: Extreme wall capacitance (C_wall = 34.6 MJ/K) stores daytime solar heat and buffers nighttime freezing.
solar_considerations: South-facing orientation with high exterior solar absorptivity (alpha = 0.75) captures intense high-altitude solar radiation.
openings_considerations: Small timber-framed double-glazed windows minimized on north face to limit infiltration losses.
construction_practicality: 100% locally sourced stone soil poplar wood and straw; zero imported material supply chain dependency.
limitations: Lacks modern continuous insulation; wall heat flow loss is moderate (1.592 W/m?K).
source_reference: Ladakh Standardized Development & Building Regulations 2023 / ISO 6946:2017

climatic_reasoning: Combines traditional high thermal mass on the interior with external thermal insulation to prevent thermal bridging and freeze-thaw degradation.
insulation_strategy: 80mm Rockwool batt (R = 2.000 m?K/W) placed on exterior side of rammed earth wall behind 20mm protective mud plaster.
thermal_mass_strategy: Interior rammed earth (300mm C = 23.0 MJ/K) remains thermally coupled to indoor space acting as internal heat sink.
solar_considerations: External dark mud plaster (alpha = 0.70) absorbs solar heat protected by exterior roof overhangs.
openings_considerations: Integrated south-facing Trombe wall / double-glazed rabsal sun-room.
construction_practicality: Uses local earth for wall structure with imported rockwool insulation batts; highly scalable for cold-region housing.
limitations: Requires weather-proof render on external rockwool layer to prevent wind washing.
source_reference: Ladakh Building Regulations 2023 Section 6 / ASHRAE 2025 Ch 26 / ISO 6946:2017

climatic_reasoning: High-performance continuous insulation meeting modern energy efficiency targets in severe sub-zero environments.
insulation_strategy: 100mm Rockwool (R = 2.500 m?K/W) plus 50mm unventilated air cavity (R = 0.210 m?K/W).
thermal_mass_strategy: 230mm CSEB block (C = 17.6 MJ/K) provides inner core thermal capacitance.
solar_considerations: Exterior CSEB block surface (alpha = 0.70) optimized for passive solar absorption.
openings_considerations: High-performance double-glazed Low-E windows with uPVC insulated frames.
construction_practicality: Utilizes local CSEB block production with standard commercial insulation products.
limitations: Requires trained labor for cavity wall tie installation and air cavity sealing.

climatic_reasoning: Designed for rapid deployment emergency relief or military high-altitude outpost shelters requiring fast heating response.
insulation_strategy: 100mm continuous XPS rigid insulation (R = 3.030 m?K/W) + 50mm air cavity (R = 0.210 m?K/W).
thermal_mass_strategy: Low internal thermal mass (C_eff = 2.1 MJ/K) enabling extremely rapid space heating with minimal auxiliary heat input.
solar_considerations: Exterior corrugated steel sheet cladding (alpha = 0.80) absorbs solar heat while protecting insulation from severe winds.
openings_considerations: Fully weather-sealed insulated door units and triple-pane glass panels.
construction_practicality: Prefabricated panel construction assembled on site in hours.
limitations: Fast cooling rate if auxiliary heating is cut off due to low thermal inertia.
source_reference: ISO 6946:2017 / Dow XPS Technical Datasheet / ASHRAE 2025

climatic_reasoning: Engineered for cold mountain conditions with high seasonal rainfall and humidity preventing interstitial condensation and moisture damage.
insulation_strategy: 120mm hydrophobic Rockwool batt (R = 3.000 m?K/W) behind 50mm ventilated drainage cavity.
thermal_mass_strategy: 250mm exterior stone masonry (C = 20.5 MJ/K) buffers temperature swings and provides mountain aesthetic integration.
solar_considerations: Pitched roof design (35?) with snow shedding and solar collector integration.
openings_considerations: Double-glazed timber-framed casement windows with weather-stripping.
construction_practicality: Standard Himachal mountain construction utilizing regional stone masons and rockwool insulation.
limitations: Requires weep holes and cavity flashings for rain drainage.
source_reference: NBC India 2016 Part 8 / ISO 6946:2017 / Rockwool DS

climatic_reasoning: Baseline conventional hot-climate construction where radiant solar reflection and natural ventilation dominate over thick winter insulation.
insulation_strategy: 50mm unventilated air cavity (R = 0.210 m?K/W) acts as thermal buffer against extreme daytime solar radiation.
thermal_mass_strategy: Moderate brick mass (C = 12.2 MJ/K) delays heat penetration during peak afternoon hours.
solar_considerations: Light reflective outer brick/plaster (alpha = 0.40 solar reflectivity 0.60) to minimize solar heat gain.
openings_considerations: Large cross-ventilation openings (2.0 ACH) to flush out accumulated heat during evening hours.
construction_practicality: Most common low-cost residential wall system in urban and peri-urban India.
limitations: Completely unsuited for high-altitude cold climates like Leh (U = 1.302 W/m?K causes high winter conductive heat loss).
